rules.status: 'current' means: the latest edition of that document held in this corpus and nothing in the corpus says it is superseded, draft or withdrawn. It does NOT assert the document is still in force in the world (that cannot be established from the document text).
rules.normative: true = the document is the issuing body's own text and states requirements with 'shall' (boilerplate 'shall not be held responsible' etc. excluded) and does not declare itself informative/voluntary. false = guidance, handbooks, best practices, reports, papers, slides, books, vocabulary-only or self-declared informative parts, and proposed rules never in force. null = held text is front matter only, so it cannot be tested. A 'shall' in a handbook or best practice is not enough: handbooks and best practices are false unless they say compliance is required.
rules.issuer: The issuing/publishing body. null for individually authored papers, slides, letters and books (publisher is not treated as issuer).
rules.edition_year: From the document's own text (or, flagged by year_basis, a corpus document that cites it, or the arXiv date for the 5 arXiv papers). Never the DB published placeholder. null when not established; year_hint_unverified then carries a title/draft claim that the held text does not confirm.
rules.supersedes_external: Documents named in this document's own text as superseded/cancelled that are not held in the corpus.
rules.evidence: chunk_id + quote; the quote is verbatim from the chunk after normalisation (remove '|' and runs of '-', private-use glyphs; collapse whitespace). Some quotes come from another document that cites this one (chunk_id says which).
